provenance: Consolidated from three validated 0sec seed-research catalogs (kernel/userland/firmware, 2023-2025 CVE-grounded). GENERALIZED PATTERNS ONLY — no specific exploit code. The kernel 'weaponization_note' field is intentionally excluded. 'grounding' lists public CVE/advisory identifiers as witnesses, not the pattern itself. See docs/SEEDS.md.

archetypes.name: nf_tables set-element deferred-free UAF (GC / async destroy / commit race)
archetypes.pattern: A set element / set backend (pipapo, rbtree, hash) is unlinked in one phase and freed by a deferred path (GC worker, call_rcu, transaction commit/abort) while another path still holds or re-walks the reference. Split unlink-vs-reclaim phases, GC-on-insert, or duplicate-element-pending-GC create a window where the freed element is reused.
archetypes.detection_signature: In a stripped nf_tables-related .ko the imported-symbol relocations survive insmod resolution: look for call_rcu / kfree_rcu / queue_delayed_work / nft_* set-ops callbacks alongside kfree of an object that is also reachable from an rcu/list walk. Decompiled shape: object unlinked from a list, then freed in a *different* function/workqueue callback than the one that still iterates it. Maps to 0verse lens L8 (deferred-free-uaf) + L12 (list-unlink). HARD in pure binary: requires cross-callback lifetime reasoning; emit as hypothesis, not a finding.
archetypes.confirmable: NO on bare binary (no live oracle for a deferred-free race). Confirmation belongs to the bench kernel-verify lane: build/boot the module under KASAN and replay the GC/commit sequence.

archetypes.name: nf_tables object/expr destroy-path UAF & error-path double-free
archetypes.pattern: Stateful object or expression (nft_tunnel, nft_ct timeout, nft_object, anonymous set bound in same transaction) is destroyed/freed on an error or abort path while another reference (binding, chain, transaction log) still points to it -> UAF, or it is freed twice across error + cleanup.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to nf_tables core (nft_obj_*, nf_tables_*destroy, module_put) survive. Decompiled shape: an init/clone function with an error label that kfree/destroys an object that the caller also frees on failure; or a _destroy callback freeing an object that a sibling _deactivate already released. Maps to L5 (refcount-asymmetry) + L6 (error-path-doublefree). MEDIUM in binary when both free sites are in the same module and one error edge is clearly shared.
archetypes.confirmable: NO on bare binary; double-free on a shared error edge is the most statically-plausible sub-case but still needs the kernel-verify lane to prove reachability.

archetypes.name: Netlink attribute parsing OOB / missing NLA length & range validation
archetypes.pattern: Attacker-supplied netlink attribute length/index/range is trusted without policy bounds: nla_parse without a min/max policy, a user range with start>end, or an option/blob length that overruns a fixed table -> heap OOB read or write at config time.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG binary signal: relocations to nla_parse / nla_parse_nested / __nla_parse / nla_get_u32 / nla_memcpy / nla_put are preserved. Decompiled shape: value loaded via nla_get_*() then used directly as memcpy length / array index / loop bound with no preceding compare against a constant cap. Maps to L1 (user-len-copy) + L3 (selector-index). HIGH detectability even stripped, because the nla_* import names cannot be stripped (module loader resolves by name).
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV on bare binary, but the bounds-missing shape is one of the most confirmable-by-inspection kernel patterns; verify in the kernel-verify lane with a crafted netlink message.

archetypes.name: nf_tables register store/load type confusion & OOB register index
archetypes.pattern: nft expressions read/write a virtual register file (nft_regs). A missing nft_validate_register_store/load check, wrong register width, or unchecked dreg/sreg index lets an expression write past the register array or reinterpret a register's type -> OOB into adjacent kernel state during rule eval.
archetypes.detection_signature: Domain-specific lens L11 (register-machine index OOB). Relocations to nft_validate_register_* survive; ABSENCE of a validate call before a register write, or a register index not masked to NFT_REG_SIZE, is the tell. MEDIUM-HARD: needs recognizing the nft register ABI in the decompile; easier with nft symbol hints.
archetypes.confirmable: NO on bare binary; kernel-verify lane with a rule that triggers the bad register access.

archetypes.name: conntrack / ctnetlink dump & refcount-underflow UAF, namespace-vs-GC race
archetypes.pattern: Dump or destroy of a conntrack/expectation/ipset object races a GC worker or netns teardown; a refcount is underflowed (put without get, or freed while a dump cursor holds it) -> UAF on a long-lived networking object.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to refcount_dec_and_test / nf_ct_put / atomic_dec preserved. Shape: a dump callback that nf_ct_get()s but releases on an early-return error path twice, or a put not paired with a get. Maps to L5 (refcount-asymmetry) + L8. HARD statically (concurrency).
grounding: ipset list:set namespace-cleanup vs GC race
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane under netns churn + KASAN.

archetypes.name: qdisc class refcount/UAF on graft/change/destroy error path
archetypes.pattern: A qdisc class (qfq, hfsc, drr, htb, cbs) is grafted/changed/deleted; an error or reset path frees or unlinks a class while the parent qdisc, an active filter, or a child qdisc still references it (e.g. child qdisc not reset before parent free). Classic refcount-on-error-path -> UAF.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to qdisc_put / qdisc_destroy / qdisc_reset / tcf_block_put survive. Shape: a *_change/*_graft function whose error label calls qdisc_destroy on an object still linked into a class hash, or a *_destroy that frees children in wrong order. Maps to L5 + L12. MEDIUM: order-of-free bugs are partly visible in the decompile.
archetypes.confirmable: NO on bare binary; kernel-verify lane with tc class manipulation + KASAN.

archetypes.name: tc classifier (cls_*) filter UAF on delete/replace
archetypes.pattern: Filter delete/replace frees a filter node or hashtable while a packet-path or another filter still references it; RCU grace handling or refcount on the filter is wrong -> UAF in classify path.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to tcf_exts_*, call_rcu, kfree_rcu, tcf_unbind_filter preserved. Shape: filter freed in a delete callback while still on an rcu-protected list reachable from classify. Maps to L8 + L5. HARD (RCU lifetime).
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: qdisc enqueue recursion / list corruption / stack overflow
archetypes.pattern: Mis-validated qdisc topology lets enqueue/dequeue recurse unboundedly or corrupt the gso/backlog list (e.g. act_mirred blockcast recursion bypass -> stack overflow; netem/peek re-entry).
archetypes.detection_signature: Shape: an enqueue path that re-invokes another qdisc's enqueue without a depth guard, or list_add/list_del on a packet list without lock. Maps to L12. HARD-MEDIUM.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: qdisc/class dump uninitialized-field info leak (data-race or padding)
archetypes.pattern: *_dump_stats / *_dump_class_stats copies a stats struct to userspace via nla_put while fields are read without locking (data-race) or struct padding is uninitialized -> kernel pointer/heap-content leak.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG binary signal: relocations to nla_put / nla_put_64bit / memset preserved. Shape: a struct filled field-by-field then nla_put'd WITHOUT a preceding memset(0) of the whole struct, or read of shared counters without READ_ONCE. Maps to L7 (uninit-copy-to-user). MEDIUM detectability (missing memset before nla_put is visible).
grounding: sch_cake/htb/hfsc/sfq/fq_codel/pie dump-stats data-race annotations (mass fix wave)
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV, but missing-memset-before-copy is statically inspectable; kernel-verify lane confirms leak content.

archetypes.name: io_uring registered buffer/file premature-free UAF
archetypes.pattern: A registered buffer, fixed file, or provided-buffer ring (pbuf_ring) is freed/unregistered while an in-flight request or mmap still references it; missing refcount or wrong unregister ordering -> page/object UAF.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to io_* core, percpu_ref_*, fput, folio_put preserved. HARD: io_uring is in-tree core (not a discrete .ko), so this archetype is mostly relevant to source/dynamic; in a vendor kernel image the io_uring code is a large static blob. Maps to L5 + L8.
grounding: CVE-2024-0582 (registered buffer leak -> page UAF -> Dirty Pipe-style write)
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: io_uring async/task_work request reuse race
archetypes.pattern: A request object is completed/freed and recycled while a concurrent task_work, poll, or cancel path still operates on it (req->task, req->file, linked SQE) -> UAF / type confusion across operations.
archetypes.detection_signature: HARD statically (concurrency, in-tree). Shape: req freed on one completion path while another path dereferences it. Maps to L9 (race) + L5.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane with stress + KASAN.

archetypes.name: eBPF verifier register-bounds / pruning miscalculation -> OOB R/W
archetypes.pattern: The verifier mis-tracks a register's value/bounds (ALU op, sign-extension, state pruning, or scalar/pointer confusion) so a program that PASSES verification performs an OOB load/store at runtime.
archetypes.detection_signature: VERY HARD in binary: the bug is in verifier *logic*, semantic, in-tree. Not a stripped-.ko pattern at all. Maps to L11 conceptually but realistically needs source + a verifier differential/fuzzer. Flag as out-of-scope for bare-binary detection.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; needs source + dynamic verifier testing.

archetypes.name: bpf map / ringbuf / helper refcount & value-copy bug
archetypes.pattern: A map element, ringbuf record, or helper-returned pointer is freed or sized wrong (off-by-one, refcount on map value across program exit) -> UAF or OOB on the map value object.
archetypes.detection_signature: HARD-MEDIUM, in-tree. Shape visible only if a discrete helper does kfree/refcount on a map value. Maps to L5.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: socket connect/release lifetime race UAF (sk vs signal/close)
archetypes.pattern: A socket struct (or sk_buff queued on it) is freed by close/release/signal-interrupted-connect while another syscall path still uses it; transport assignment or GC ordering is racy.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to sock_put / __sk_destruct / skb_free / kfree_skb / lock_sock survive. HARD (concurrency). Shape: sk dereferenced after a lock_sock-released window, or transport freed on signal path. Maps to L9 + L5.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane. (bench has kernel-hack-drill-style harnesses for exactly this class.)

archetypes.name: sockmap / sk_psock / kcm recvmsg-sendmsg sk_buff sharing UAF
archetypes.pattern: An skb/sk_msg is shared between a psock backlog and the receive path; partial recv, MSG_PEEK, redirect, or unattach frees or re-queues the buffer while still referenced -> UAF.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to sk_psock_*, skb_clone, kfree_skb, sk_msg_* survive. HARD (concurrency + queue lifetime). Shape: skb freed in one queue path while linked in another. Maps to L8 + L12.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane. bench has the kcm baseline + skmsg-lpe harness already.

archetypes.name: setsockopt/getsockopt optlen OOB / sockptr copy confusion
archetypes.pattern: optlen from userspace is trusted: copy_from_sockptr of attacker length into a fixed buffer, or getsockopt writing more than the user buffer, or a signed/unsigned optlen confusion -> stack/heap OOB.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG: relocations to copy_from_sockptr / copy_to_sockptr / copy_from_user / put_user survive. Shape: copy sized by a user-provided optlen with no clamp to sizeof(local). Maps to L1. HIGH detectability.
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV, but bounded-copy-missing is statically inspectable; kernel-verify lane confirms.

archetypes.name: minor-protocol list/queue UAF & race (CAN bcm, n_gsm, tipc, nfc, bluetooth)
archetypes.pattern: Less-audited protocols mismanage a per-socket list/timer/fragment-reassembly buffer on teardown or concurrent op -> UAF / double-free / OOB. These are reachable by unprivileged users and historically under-fuzzed.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to del_timer / hrtimer_cancel / list_del / kfree_skb / call_rcu survive. Shape: timer or list entry freed but not removed, or reassembly buffer reused. Maps to L5/L8/L12. MEDIUM-HARD.
grounding: tipc / nfc-llcp / nfc-digital / bluetooth fixes (0sec-disclosed, merged)
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: On-disk / image metadata parsing OOB (untrusted filesystem mount)
archetypes.subsystem: fs (ext4, ntfs3, hfs/hfsplus, udf, f2fs, squashfs)
archetypes.pattern: A filesystem driver trusts on-disk length/offset/count fields when parsing superblock/inode/dirent metadata; a crafted image overruns a buffer or integer-overflows an allocation. Reachable via USB-stick/loopback mount or (in some distros) unprivileged automount.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG for the fs .ko: relocations to sb_bread / kmalloc / memcpy / le16_to_cpu / le32_to_cpu survive. Shape: a length read from buffer_head data via le*_to_cpu used as memcpy size / loop bound / kmalloc size without sanity bound. Maps to L1 + L2. HIGH detectability in a fs module.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: a corpus of crafted images can be replayed in the kernel-verify lane (mount under KASAN) -- one of the more PoV-able kernel classes. Bare-binary stays hypothesis.

archetypes.name: overlayfs / FUSE copy-up credential & permission confusion
archetypes.pattern: Copy-up or revalidation runs with the wrong cred (mounter vs caller), or a check is performed on the lower and use on the upper (TOCTOU), letting an unprivileged user gain access/setuid semantics they shouldn't.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to override_creds / revert_creds / prepare_creds / inode_permission survive. Shape: an operation bracketed by override_creds(mounter_cred) that performs a user-influenced path op. Maps to L4 (missing/wrong cap-gate) + L9. MEDIUM.
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV on bare binary; kernel-verify lane with a layered mount.

archetypes.name: VFS/ioctl path TOCTOU & symlink/mount-point race
archetypes.pattern: A filesystem checks a path/inode property then acts on it after a window in which the attacker swaps a symlink/mount/file (double-fetch of a user path, or re-resolved dentry).
archetypes.detection_signature: HARD: races are not visible as a single decompiled shape. Look for a user-pointer read twice (double-fetch) -- copy_from_user of the same uaddr in a check and a use. Maps to L9. LOW-MEDIUM detectability (double-fetch is the only statically visible sub-case).
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane with a racing thread.

archetypes.name: pipe_buffer / page-cache uninitialized-flag write (Dirty Pipe family)
archetypes.pattern: A pipe_buffer's flags (PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE) or a page-cache page state is left from a prior use, letting a splice/write merge into a read-only or shared page -> write to data the caller shouldn't write.
archetypes.detection_signature: HARD in binary (in-tree mm, subtle state init). Shape: a struct/flag field reused without reset before a merge/write decision. Maps to L7-adjacent (uninit-state). LOW detectability.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; but the *exploitation* of an unrelated page-UAF INTO this primitive is a known recipe.

archetypes.name: COW / page-table / hugepage race write (Dirty COW / Dirty Pagetable)
archetypes.pattern: A race in copy-on-write fault handling or page-table teardown lets a write land in a shared/read-only page or lets a freed page be reused as a page-table -> arbitrary physical write.
archetypes.detection_signature: VERY HARD (core mm, concurrency). Out-of-scope for bare-binary; listed for completeness as an exploitation TARGET primitive.
archetypes.confirmable: NO.

archetypes.name: uninitialized kernel allocation copied to user (heap/stack infoleak)
archetypes.pattern: kmalloc (not __GFP_ZERO) or an on-stack struct with padding is partially filled then copied to userspace -> leak of prior heap contents / kernel pointers.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG generic signal: relocations to copy_to_user / put_user / nla_put paired with kmalloc (no kzalloc) and NO memset of the buffer. Shape: alloc -> set some fields -> copy_to_user(size==full struct). Maps to L7. HIGH detectability across ALL modules; the cheapest, most common find.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: the missing-zero shape is statically strong; kernel-verify lane confirms which bytes leak.

archetypes.name: ioctl dispatch: unchecked user selector index into handler/array
archetypes.pattern: An ioctl cmd or a user-supplied index selects a handler from a function-pointer table or reads/writes an array element without bounding the index against the table size -> OOB call or OOB array access.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG and the SINGLE most binary-detectable kernel class: in a stripped .ko, an .unlocked_ioctl/.ioctl fop is a switch or a `table[arg]` indirect call. Relocations to copy_from_user (to read the arg struct) survive. Shape: value from user used as index/offset with no `cmp idx, CONST; ja` guard before an indexed load/indirect-call. Maps to L3 (ioctl-selector-index). HIGH detectability even fully stripped -- the fops struct and the indexed indirect call are visible.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: reachability is clear from the fops table; a PoV needs the device node + kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: ioctl/write copy_from_user with attacker-controlled length into fixed buffer
archetypes.pattern: copy_from_user(dst, uptr, len) where len comes from the user (ioctl arg field, write() count, header length) and dst is a fixed-size stack or heap buffer with no clamp -> overflow.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG: relocations to copy_from_user / _copy_from_user / memdup_user / strncpy_from_user survive insmod. Shape: the 3rd arg to copy_from_user traces back to a user-loaded value, and dst is a fixed stack slot (sub rsp,N) or a fixed kmalloc(CONST). Absence of a `cmp len, CONST` clamp is the tell. Maps to L1 (user-len-copy). HIGH detectability stripped.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: shape is statically strong; PoV via device node in kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: allocation-size integer overflow (count * size) from user input
archetypes.pattern: kmalloc/kvmalloc/vmalloc/kcalloc size computed as a*b or a+b from user-controlled count and element size; the multiply overflows to a small allocation, then a loop writes `count` elements -> heap overflow. Includes missing use of array_size()/struct_size()/check_mul_overflow.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG: relocations to kmalloc / kvmalloc / vmalloc / kmalloc_array preserved. Shape: an `imul`/`shl`/`add` of two non-constant (user-traced) operands feeding the size arg of an allocator, WITHOUT a preceding overflow check (no call to __builtin_mul_overflow inline / no compare). Maps to L2 (alloc-size-arith). HIGH detectability -- the arithmetic-before-alloc pattern is visible in the decompile.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: static shape strong; kernel-verify lane confirms the undersize+overflow.

archetypes.name: missing capable()/ns_capable() gate on a privileged operation
archetypes.pattern: A privileged ioctl/sysfs-store/debugfs/write handler (firmware load, register poke, DMA setup, mode switch) lacks a capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)/ns_capable/perm check, so an unprivileged user reaches a powerful primitive directly.
archetypes.detection_signature: STRONG and high-value: in the .ko, the PRESENCE of a powerful sink (writel/iowrite, dma_alloc, request_firmware, copy_*_user to phys) on a path that has NO relocation to capable / ns_capable / capable_wrt_inode is the signal. Maps to L4 (missing-cap-gate). HIGH detectability: 0verse can diff `paths-to-sink` against `paths-through-capable`. Absence-of-a-call is exactly what survives stripping (the capable import would be there if used).
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: the missing-check is statically strong; exploit value depends on the sink.

archetypes.name: shared-object refcount underflow across fd/mmap (Binder, DRM, dma-buf)
archetypes.pattern: An object shared between processes via fd/handle/mmap has a refcount that can be under-incremented or double-decremented (handle table races, mmap close vs ioctl) -> UAF on a long-lived, sprayable driver object.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to kref_get/kref_put / refcount_inc/refcount_dec_and_test / dma_buf_put / drm_gem_object_put survive. Shape: a put without a matching get on some path, or a handle freed while mmapped. Maps to L5 (refcount-asymmetry). MEDIUM (some imbalance visible; races need dynamic).
grounding: Android Binder refcount UAFs (repeated ITW exploitation)
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane (or device emulation).

archetypes.name: double-free / use-after-free on driver probe/error/cleanup path
archetypes.pattern: An init/probe/reset routine frees a resource on an error label that the caller (or a later cleanup) also frees, or frees-then-uses; tangled goto-error ladders are the classic source.
archetypes.detection_signature: MEDIUM: relocations to kfree / kvfree / free_irq / dma_free preserved. Shape: the same pointer passed to kfree on two reachable paths, or kfree followed by a deref of the same register. Maps to L6 (error-path-doublefree). MEDIUM detectability -- intra-function double-free is one of the few UAFs statically visible.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL: intra-function double-free is statically inspectable; cross-function needs the lane.

archetypes.name: TOCTOU double-fetch of user pointer in ioctl
archetypes.pattern: An ioctl reads a length/count from the user struct, validates it, then copies again from the SAME user address (or a sub-pointer) which the attacker changes in between -> validated-then-larger copy -> overflow.
archetypes.detection_signature: MEDIUM-STRONG (rare among races): two copy_from_user calls reading the same uaddr, with a bound-check on the first value but the copy sized by a re-fetched value. Relocations to copy_from_user/get_user survive; the DOUBLE read of one uaddr is the static tell. Maps to L9 + L1. The most statically-detectable race sub-class.
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV without a racing thread; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: DMA / mmap region with insufficient bounds -> arbitrary phys/IO access
archetypes.pattern: A driver maps device/DMA memory to userspace (mmap fop) or programs a DMA descriptor using a user-supplied offset/size without bounding it to the allocated region -> user gets read/write to arbitrary physical or adjacent kernel memory.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to remap_pfn_range / dma_alloc_coherent / io_remap_pfn_range / vm_iomap_memory survive. Shape: an mmap fop where vma->vm_pgoff (user-controlled) feeds the pfn without a range clamp, or a DMA addr/len from user. Maps to L1/L3. MEDIUM-HIGH (mmap fop + remap_pfn_range with unclamped pgoff is a clear shape).
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV on bare binary; kernel-verify lane with the device.

archetypes.name: keyring / key refcount UAF (request_key_auth, keyctl)
archetypes.pattern: A key or key_ref refcount is mishandled on an error/assoc path (request_key_auth UAF, key GC vs use) -> UAF on a key object reachable from an unprivileged keyctl call.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to key_put / key_ref_put / refcount_dec survive. Shape: put-without-get or use-after-put on a key. Maps to L5 + L8. MEDIUM-HARD.
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane (bench has the keyctl harness).

archetypes.name: SysV IPC / msg_msg OOB or UAF (bug-bearing OR reclaim object)
archetypes.pattern: An IPC object (msg_msg segment list, shm) is mis-sized or freed early. Note dual role: msg_msg is BOTH a recurring bug location AND the universal heap-spray/reclaim object used to exploit other UAFs.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to kmalloc/kfree in ipc paths; msg_msg segment loop with a user-controlled msgsz feeding alloc. Maps to L2/L5. MEDIUM. (For 0verse, the higher value is recognizing msg_msg as the EXPLOIT PRIMITIVE that confirms many other UAFs in the verify lane.)
grounding: msg_msg as exploitation primitive across most UAF writeups
archetypes.confirmable: NO; kernel-verify lane.

archetypes.name: perf/ptrace/cred & namespace privilege confusion
archetypes.pattern: A privilege/capability check is performed against the wrong cred or namespace (init_user_ns vs current_user_ns), or a cred transition is mis-ordered, granting capabilities the caller shouldn't have. User-namespace reachability is what makes many of the above archetypes unprivileged.
archetypes.detection_signature: Relocations to ns_capable / capable / current_cred / make_kuid survive. Shape: capable() used where ns_capable(target_ns) is required, or a check against init_user_ns for a namespaced resource. Maps to L4. MEDIUM (requires knowing the right ns).
archetypes.confirmable: NO PoV on bare binary; semantic.

archetypes.name: Header length field used as copy/read size without validation
archetypes.pattern: A length/size/count field is read straight out of an attacker-controlled file or packet header, then passed as the size argument to memcpy/memmove/read/strncpy into a buffer whose capacity was decided independently (fixed or from a different field). No 'len <= cap' check sits between the parse and the copy.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: memcpy/memmove/__memcpy_chk/read/fread/recv. Decompiled shape: a value loaded from the parse cursor (ptr+const, or a struct field at a fixed offset just after a magic/tag compare) flows as arg3 of memcpy with no min/clamp in the dominator path. Slice: backward taint from memcpy.size to a file/socket read; lens fires when the source is attacker-reachable AND no comparison node (jle/jbe against the destination's allocation size) dominates the call. SHARPENING (overflow lens): add the 'size-operand provenance' check — flag when memcpy.size traces to a load, not a compile-time constant or a value the allocator was sized from; treat a clamp only as valid if it bounds against the SAME symbol used for the dest allocation.
grounding: CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp VP8L Huffman table OOB write)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: craft input with a length field larger than the real payload / dest capacity; redzone page or guard between allocations catches the OOB write deterministically, CASR classifies as heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.
archetypes.fp_trap: A bounded copy where a clamp like 'if (len > cap) len = cap;' or 'min(len, remaining)' precedes the memcpy — suppress when a comparison against the dest's own size symbol dominates the sink. Also suppress when size is a struct sizeof() constant.

archetypes.name: Decompressed/expanded size exceeds buffer sized from compressed/declared size
archetypes.pattern: Output buffer is allocated from a declared/uncompressed-size field (or from the compressed length), but the actual decode loop writes until an end marker or run-length count, which can exceed the allocation. Classic in RLE/LZ/Huffman/predictor decoders and image upsamplers.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: memcpy/memset in a loop, or byte-store in a decode loop with a writer cursor. Decompiled shape: alloc(N) where N is a header field; a loop store *dst++ = ... bounded by a separately-derived counter (run length, code length) not re-checked against dst_end. Slice: detect a store whose pointer is monotonically advanced in a loop with no 'dst < dst_end' guard tied to the allocation size. SHARPENING (overflow lens): add a loop-writer lens variant — track the write cursor vs allocation end across loop back-edges, not just single straight-line memcpy; flag decode loops where the bound counter is independent of the dst capacity.
grounding: CVE-2023-4863 (libwebp lossless lookup tables written before validity check)
CVE-2024-20697 (Windows libarchive RCE via crafted archive)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: input whose declared size is small but whose decode stream expands past it (unbalanced Huffman / long RLE run). Guard page catches the loop write overrun.
archetypes.fp_trap: Decoders that re-clamp the writer each iteration ('if (dst >= dst_end) break;') or grow the buffer with realloc keyed to the writer position — suppress when a dst_end comparison gates the store in the loop body.

archetypes.name: Stale/mis-set flag causes the long source (not the short one) to be copied
archetypes.pattern: A control variable decides whether a SHORT canonical value (e.g. a resolved address, a truncated name) or the LONG raw input is copied into a fixed buffer. A logic/state bug leaves the flag wrong on a slow/partial path, so the long input is memcpy'd into the buffer sized for the short one.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: memcpy/strcpy into a fixed/stack buffer. Decompiled shape: two assignments to the copy-source under different branches of a boolean that is itself set far away (across a state-machine step / I/O resumption). Slice: dataflow where memcpy.src can be either a bounded constant or an unbounded input depending on a flag whose definition does not dominate the use. SHARPENING (overflow lens): flag 'phi-source' memcpys where one incoming source is length-bounded and another is not, and the selecting predicate is set across a callback/resume boundary (harder for pure static tools — 0verse can just fuzz the state machine to flip it).
grounding: CVE-2023-38545 (curl SOCKS5 long-hostname heap overflow via wrong local-resolve flag)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: drive the slow/partial-handshake path with an over-long input; the flag misfires and the over-length memcpy hits the redzone. Confirmable but needs the state-machine condition (slow handshake) — note as 'needs protocol stepping'.
archetypes.fp_trap: Cases where every branch that selects the long source also sizes/checks the buffer accordingly — suppress when the long-source branch is dominated by a length check against dest capacity.

archetypes.name: Attacker string copied into fixed stack/struct buffer (unbounded string op)
archetypes.pattern: Attacker-controlled NUL-terminated string is copied into a fixed-size stack array or struct member with strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets/scanf(%s) — no length cap, no -n variant. Bound is the source's NUL, not the destination's capacity.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: strcpy/strcat/sprintf/vsprintf/gets/__isoc99_scanf/stpcpy. Decompiled shape: dest is a stack slot (rbp-relative, fixed size known from the frame) or a struct field; src traces to argv/getenv/recv/fread. Slice: any unbounded string sink whose dest has a statically known smaller-than-source-bound size. SHARPENING (overflow lens): ensure the sink list includes the often-missed stpcpy, strlcat-misuse (return value ignored), and sprintf with %s; treat sprintf/snprintf where the format's %s width is unbounded as equivalent to strcpy. Taint-source set must include getenv and the full argv[] vector, not just network reads.
archetypes.confirmable: canary (stack) + CASR for stack smashing; differential-allocator + CASR for heap/struct. Trigger: oversize the input string past the frame buffer; stack canary trips or CASR reports stack-buffer-overflow.
archetypes.fp_trap: strncpy/snprintf/strlcpy with a correct size argument; or a preceding strlen()+compare against capacity. Suppress when a length check on the source dominates the unbounded sink, OR when the bounded variant is used with the dest's sizeof().

archetypes.name: Off-by-one in NUL-termination / index loop
archetypes.pattern: A copy/loop writes exactly capacity bytes then also writes a terminating NUL at buf[len] == buf[cap] (one past), or uses '<=' instead of '<' as the loop bound, or strncpy fills the buffer with no room for the terminator and a later 'buf[n]=0' lands out of bounds.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: single-byte store at buf[i] where i can equal the allocation size; or strncpy(dst,src,sizeof(dst)) followed by dst[sizeof(dst)]=0. Decompiled shape: loop with cmp using <= / a terminator store at an index equal to the size constant. Slice: detect a store at index == known_capacity, or a terminator write whose index is the same constant passed to the preceding bounded copy. SHARPENING (overflow lens): add an explicit 'one-past' rule — when a bounded copy uses size S and a NUL store uses index S (not S-1) on the same buffer, raise; current overflow lens keyed on big overruns can miss single-byte writes.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR (heap, 1-byte redzone hit) or canary (stack). Trigger: input of length exactly == capacity so the terminator/last write lands one past. Reliable with a tight redzone allocator.
archetypes.fp_trap: Buffers deliberately sized cap+1 for the terminator. Suppress when the allocation size is provably len+1 relative to the loop bound, or when the terminator index is bound-1.

archetypes.name: Pixel/sample buffer written with different dimensions than it was allocated for
archetypes.pattern: Buffer allocated as width*height*bpp from one set of header fields, but the fill/scan loop iterates using a different (later-parsed, larger, or per-strip) dimension, or stride/rowbytes computed inconsistently. Common in TIFF/JPEG/PNG strip & tile decoders.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: row/scanline store loop, memcpy per row. Decompiled shape: alloc uses dims A; nested loop bound uses dims B (different field loads) or stride S not equal to alloc row size. Slice: compare the symbols feeding the allocation size against the symbols feeding the loop bounds/stride; mismatch with attacker control on either side raises. SHARPENING (overflow lens): add a 'dimension-consistency' check linking alloc-size provenance to loop-bound provenance; flag when width/height used for alloc differ (by symbol identity) from those used in the write loop.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: header with inconsistent dims (e.g. small alloc dim, large loop dim). Guard catches the row overrun; CASR shows WRITE OOB.
archetypes.fp_trap: Decoders that recompute and validate stride == alloc_rowbytes, or re-allocate per strip. Suppress when a check ties loop dims back to the allocation dims.

archetypes.name: Loop appends N attacker-counted entries into a fixed-capacity array
archetypes.pattern: A count field from input drives a loop that stores into a fixed-size array (table of pointers, descriptor array, ID list) without checking the running index against capacity. Out-of-bounds element write.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: store to base + index*elemsize in a loop. Decompiled shape: loop counter bounded by an attacker count; store into a buffer of fixed element capacity; no 'index < CAP' guard. Slice: indexed write where the index bound is attacker-derived and the base allocation is fixed/constant. SHARPENING (overflow lens / index sub-lens): track array-index writes (base+i*sz) separately from byte memcpy; flag when i's upper bound is attacker-controlled and the base size is constant.
grounding: CVE-2024-37079 (vCenter DCERPC array, integer-underflow feeding count)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: oversize the count field. Element store past the array end hits the redzone.
archetypes.fp_trap: Loops with 'if (n > MAX) n = MAX;' or 'for (i=0; i<n && i<CAP; i++)'. Suppress when the loop condition conjoins a capacity bound.

archetypes.name: memcpy/alloc size from subtraction that underflows (len = total - offset)
archetypes.pattern: Size computed as A - B (remaining = total_len - consumed, or end - start) where B can exceed A, wrapping an unsigned subtraction to a near-SIZE_MAX value used as a copy length, causing a massive OOB read/write.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: memcpy/memmove with size = sub result. Decompiled shape: size operand is the result of a 'sub' whose operands are both attacker-influenced (or one parsed offset) with no 'B <= A' check before the subtract. Slice: backward from memcpy.size to a subtraction node; raise if no guard ensures minuend >= subtrahend. SHARPENING (overflow + intoverflow bridge): add 'unsigned-subtraction-as-size' detector — when a size operand is a sub and the subtrahend lacks an upper-bound check vs the minuend, flag; this is a high-yield shape pure-size-constant checks miss.
grounding: CVE-2024-37079 (VMware vCenter integer underflow -> code exec)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: input where consumed/offset > total so the subtraction wraps; copy of ~SIZE_MAX faults immediately (CASR: SEGV / huge memcpy). Strongly confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that checks 'if (consumed > total) goto err;' before computing remaining. Suppress when a >= guard on the subtraction operands dominates the sink.

archetypes.name: sprintf format-expansion overflow (output longer than fixed buffer)
archetypes.pattern: sprintf/vsprintf builds a string (path, command, log line, URL) into a fixed buffer; one or more %s/%d expansions from attacker data make the result exceed the buffer even though each piece looked 'small'. Not a format-string bug (format is trusted) — it is a length bug.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: sprintf/vsprintf (no size bound). Decompiled shape: format literal with %s/%d, dest is fixed-size, at least one argument is attacker-tainted with unbounded length. Slice: sprintf where dest capacity < worst-case expansion of a tainted %s argument. SHARPENING (overflow lens): treat every sprintf/vsprintf into a fixed buffer with a tainted %s as an overflow candidate, distinct from the fmtstring lens (which only cares about attacker-controlled FORMAT). Two different lenses must both watch the printf family for different reasons.
grounding: CVE-2023-6246 (glibc __vsyslog_internal heap overflow building the log line)
archetypes.confirmable: canary/CASR (stack) or differential-allocator/CASR (heap). Trigger: make a tainted %s argument long enough that the formatted output overruns the dest.
archetypes.fp_trap: snprintf with correct size, or dest sized from a prior strlen-sum. Suppress when dest is provably >= sum of max argument lengths + literal.

archetypes.name: realloc growth pattern with retained/under-sized state
archetypes.pattern: A dynamic buffer grows via realloc, but the capacity bookkeeping is wrong (off-by-one in the grow condition, or the new size is computed before adding the incoming chunk), so a subsequent write exceeds the actual allocation. (Distinct from the UAF realloc-stale-pointer case.)
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: store after realloc; the running 'used' vs 'cap' tracking. Decompiled shape: realloc(p, newcap) where newcap < used+incoming, then memcpy(p+used, in, incoming). Slice: detect grow-then-append where the grow size does not account for the appended length. SHARPENING (overflow lens): model a 'cap/used' pair around realloc sites; flag append memcpys where incoming length is not added into the realloc size argument.
grounding: libarchive RAR window realloc class (CWE-122 adjacent)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: feed chunks that force a grow where the new size is undercomputed; the append overruns. Confirmable but may need multiple chunks to reach the bad grow.
archetypes.fp_trap: Correct 'while (used+incoming > cap) cap *= 2; realloc(p,cap);' patterns. Suppress when the realloc size demonstrably includes the incoming length.

archetypes.name: Allocation size = count * elem_size with no multiplication-overflow check
archetypes.pattern: malloc(count * size) (or malloc(n * sizeof(T))) where count comes from input; the product wraps a 32/64-bit size_t to a small value, a small buffer is allocated, then count elements are written -> heap overflow. The canonical CWE-680 (integer overflow to buffer overflow).
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: malloc/realloc with a 'mul' size operand; followed by a write loop of 'count' elements. Decompiled shape: imul feeding the alloc size; at least one factor is a tainted load; no prior check that count <= SIZE_MAX/size. Slice: alloc-size = mul(tainted, k) with no overflow guard, paired with a count-bounded write loop. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): explicitly recognize malloc(a*b) vs calloc(a,b) — calloc is overflow-safe, raw malloc(mul) is not; flag the malloc/realloc-of-product shape and DOWNGRADE if the code is calloc or has a 'count > MAX/size' guard. Add the write-loop pairing as the confirmable amplifier.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: count/size whose product wraps (e.g. count near 2^32/size on 32-bit, or 2^64/size). Tiny alloc + full write loop overruns -> CASR heap-buffer-overflow. HIGHLY confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: calloc(count,size); or an explicit 'if (count > SIZE_MAX/size) fail;' guard; or 64-bit math where the product cannot realistically wrap. Suppress on calloc and on a divide-based overflow guard.

archetypes.name: Additive size overflow (len1 + len2 + hdr) wraps before allocation
archetypes.pattern: A buffer size is the sum of several attacker-influenced lengths (header + payload + padding). The addition wraps to a small value; allocation is small; the components are then copied in full -> overflow.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: alloc with an 'add' size operand fed by 2+ tainted lengths; subsequent memcpys of each component. Decompiled shape: add chain into malloc size; components later used individually as memcpy sizes whose sum exceeds the (wrapped) allocation. Slice: alloc-size = sum(tainted...) with no saturating/overflow check; correlate with per-component copies. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): track additive size expressions, not only multiplicative; flag when the sum of later copy lengths can exceed the allocation due to wrap.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: lengths whose sum wraps; first or second component copy overruns the undersized buffer.
archetypes.fp_trap: Checked addition (compiler __builtin_add_overflow, or 'if (a > MAX - b) fail'). Suppress when an overflow-aware guard dominates.

archetypes.name: Signed/unsigned confusion bypasses a length bounds check
archetypes.pattern: A length is read into a signed int and checked 'if (len > MAX) reject', but a negative len passes the check, then is passed to memcpy/read where it is reinterpreted as a huge size_t. Or 'numeric range comparison without minimum check' (CWE-839): only the upper bound is tested.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: memcpy/read/malloc with a size operand that is a sign-extended/converted value. Decompiled shape: a signed comparison (jg/jl, movsx) gates the path, but the sink uses the value as unsigned (size_t). Slice: detect a value compared with a SIGNED predicate then consumed in an UNSIGNED context (movsxd before the call), with only an upper-bound check. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): add the 'signed-check / unsigned-use' detector keyed on movsx/movsxd between the compare and the sink, and on the absence of a 'len >= 0' (lower-bound) guard. This is a top-yield, low-FP shape that pure size-constant lenses miss entirely.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: supply a negative (or >2^31) length that passes the signed upper-bound check; the unsigned sink reads/writes a huge region -> immediate SEGV/overflow. Strongly confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that uses unsigned types throughout, or checks both 'len >= 0 && len <= MAX'. Suppress when a lower-bound (>=0) check or an unsigned-typed compare dominates.

archetypes.name: Integer truncation: wide length narrowed (64->32 / size_t->int) before alloc
archetypes.pattern: A 64-bit or size_t length is truncated to a narrower type (int/uint16/uint32) for the allocation, but the full-width value is used for the copy (or vice-versa). The alloc is small, the copy is large.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: alloc takes a narrowed value (mov eax then movzx/and), copy uses the full register. Decompiled shape: a 64-bit load truncated (movsxd/and 0xffffffff/movzx) on the alloc path but full on the copy path. Slice: detect width-mismatch between the alloc-size def and the copy-size def of the same logical length. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): add a 'width-narrowing' check — when a single tainted length reaches both an allocation and a copy but through different register widths/truncations, flag.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: length whose low 32 bits are small but high bits set (e.g. 0x1_0000_0040); 32-bit alloc small, 64-bit copy huge -> overflow.
archetypes.fp_trap: Consistent widths throughout, or a check that the value fits the narrow type before truncating. Suppress when a 'value <= UINT32_MAX' guard precedes the narrowing.

archetypes.name: Shift / type-promotion overflow in a size computation
archetypes.pattern: Size derived via left-shift (1 << n, count << bpp_shift) or via promotion of small types (uint16*uint16 promoted to int and overflowing), where the shift amount or factors are attacker-controlled, producing a wrapped/negative size.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: alloc with a 'shl' or promoted-product size operand. Decompiled shape: shl by a tainted/loaded count, or imul of two sub-int loads, feeding the size. Slice: alloc-size provenance includes shl with tainted shift, or a promotion that can exceed the target type. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): include shift-based and promotion-based size expressions in the integer-overflow lens, not only explicit mul/add.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: large shift amount or factor combination that wraps the size; undersized alloc + full write.
archetypes.fp_trap: Shifts with statically bounded amounts (masked to a few bits) that cannot overflow. Suppress when the shift amount is range-limited by a preceding mask/check.

archetypes.name: Integer underflow on a counter/length used as an index or size
archetypes.pattern: An unsigned counter is decremented past zero (len-- in a loop, remaining -= consumed) wrapping to a huge value that then drives a loop bound or index, yielding OOB. Distinct from OF-08 in that the wrap happens via repeated/conditional decrement, not a single subtract.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: loop bound or index = an unsigned variable that was decremented. Decompiled shape: 'dec'/'sub' on an unsigned counter inside a loop with no underflow guard, the counter then used as a memcpy size or array index. Slice: detect monotone decrement of an unsigned size with a use after it can reach 0 and wrap. SHARPENING (intoverflow lens): pair with OF-08; add underflow tracking on loop-carried length/counter variables.
grounding: CVE-2022-37434 (zlib inflate length underflow, header processing)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: input that causes one extra decrement (e.g. consumed > remaining) so the counter wraps; subsequent huge loop faults.
archetypes.fp_trap: Counters guarded by 'if (remaining < consumed) break;' before the decrement. Suppress when an underflow guard dominates the decrement.

archetypes.name: Attacker-controlled string used as the printf-family FORMAT argument
archetypes.pattern: User/network/file data flows directly into the format-string parameter of printf/fprintf/sprintf/snprintf/vprintf, e.g. printf(user) instead of printf("%s", user). Enables info leak (%x/%p/%s) and, with %n, an arbitrary write.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: printf/fprintf/sprintf/snprintf/vprintf/vfprintf/dprintf. Decompiled shape: the FORMAT argument register (rdi for printf, rsi for fprintf, etc.) is a tainted pointer, not a string literal in .rodata. Slice: check whether the format-arg points into a read-only literal; if it traces to argv/getenv/recv/fread, fire. SHARPENING (fmtstring lens): precisely model the format-arg POSITION per function (printf=arg0, fprintf/dprintf=arg1, snprintf=arg2, syslog=arg1, err/warn=arg0/varies) so taint is checked on the RIGHT operand; include the *_chk fortified variants and dprintf/asprintf. FP-suppress when the format operand is a .rodata pointer.
grounding: CVE-2024-29510 (Ghostscript format string -> SAFER bypass / RCE)
archetypes.confirmable: CASR (with %n: SEGV/controlled write) + differential behavior. Trigger: feed a format payload (e.g. '%n%n%n' or '%99999d%n'); a crash or detectable write confirms. Info-leak-only variants are observable via output but the WRITE variant is cleanly oracle-confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: Wrapper functions that pass a CONSTANT format and forward user data as an argument (printf("%s", user)). Suppress when the format operand is a literal; only fire when the format pointer itself is tainted.

archetypes.name: Attacker data as format to logging/err helpers (syslog/err/warn/verr)
archetypes.pattern: Same as FS-01 but via logging and error helpers that take a format: syslog(pri, user), err/errx/warn/warnx/verr, g_log/g_printerr, custom log(fmt,...) wrappers. Often overlooked because the call looks like 'just logging'.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: syslog/__syslog_chk/err/errx/warn/warnx/verr/vsyslog, plus resolvable custom log wrappers (a function whose Nth arg reaches an internal vprintf). Decompiled shape: the format-position arg is tainted. Slice: same as FS-01 with the logging-function format positions. SHARPENING (fmtstring lens): EXTEND the sink set beyond raw printf to syslog/err/warn families and to user-defined variadic log wrappers (detect by 'arg flows to v*printf inside the callee'). This is the most common real-world format-string locus and a frequent miss.
grounding: CVE-2012-... CUPS/printer daemons syslog class (generalized to recent printer CVEs)
archetypes.confirmable: CASR. Trigger: input containing %n/%s reaches the log call; crash or write confirms. Note: requires the log level/path to actually be emitted (some logs gated by verbosity) — flag as 'needs log path enabled'.
archetypes.fp_trap: Logging calls with a constant format and user data as a trailing %s arg. Suppress when format is a literal.

archetypes.name: %n write-primitive / format string used to defeat a sandbox or hijack control
archetypes.pattern: A reachable format-string bug containing %n (or positional %k$n) is leveraged for an arbitrary memory write — to corrupt a function pointer, GOT entry, saved return, or a security flag (e.g. Ghostscript's SAFER state). The distinguishing feature is a WRITE conversion in attacker-controlled format.
archetypes.detection_signature: Same sinks as FS-01/02, plus a heuristic that the tainted format can contain conversion specifiers reaching %n. Decompiled shape: tainted format-arg + the binary uses libc printf that supports %n (not hardened with FORTIFY %n-in-writable-format rejection). Slice: FS-01 taint + a note on whether _FORTIFY_SOURCE/%n protection is present (glibc rejects %n in writable-segment format strings under FORTIFY). SHARPENING (fmtstring lens): add a confidence boost when the target binary's printf is NOT fortified (no __printf_chk imports) — %n is then live; downgrade if __*_chk dominates and the format is in a writable segment (glibc will abort).
archetypes.confirmable: CASR. Trigger: a positional %n payload writing to a mapped address; the controlled write/crash is oracle-visible. Among the most cleanly confirmable archetypes for a userland PoV.
archetypes.fp_trap: Hardened builds where glibc FORTIFY aborts on %n in a writable-segment format (the abort is a DoS, not a write primitive). Distinguish abort() from a controlled write in CASR classification.

archetypes.name: Free on an error/early branch, then use after the branches merge
archetypes.pattern: An object is freed in one branch (error handling, early-out, retry) but the pointer is not nulled; control merges and a later access (read/write/free) touches the freed object. The most common userland UAF.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: load/store/free through a pointer P after a free(P) on a dominating-or-sibling path with no intervening reassignment/NULL. Decompiled shape: free(P) in a branch; P used at a post-dominator without a new def. Slice: alias-aware liveness — flag a use of P that is reachable from a free(P) with no redefinition in between. SHARPENING (uaf lens): ensure the lens models the 'free-then-merge' control shape (free in one predecessor of a join, use at/after the join) and does not require the free and use to be straight-line; track pointer nulling as the suppressor.
grounding: CVE-2023-0286-class (OpenSSL X.400 type confusion -> UAF, generalized)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: drive the error branch that frees, then the path that uses. Differential allocator quarantines freed chunks so the post-free access is a deterministic UAF read/write, CASR classifies as heap-use-after-free. HIGHLY confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that sets P = NULL after free (and checks for NULL before use), or reassigns P. Suppress when a NULL-store to P dominates the later use, or the use is guarded by 'if (P)'.

archetypes.name: Double-free in goto-fail / cleanup chains
archetypes.pattern: Error-cleanup code frees an object, and a second cleanup label (or the caller's cleanup) frees it again because ownership was not cleared. Common with cascading 'goto err' labels and shared cleanup functions.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: free(P) reachable from another free(P) with no reassignment. Decompiled shape: two free(P) calls on a path (often via fallthrough goto labels) with P unchanged. Slice: detect two frees of the same allocation on a feasible path. SHARPENING (uaf lens): add explicit double-free detection (free reaching free), and recognize the goto-label fallthrough pattern where multiple cleanup labels free overlapping sets; track 'freed' as a state to suppress when P is nulled between.
grounding: CVE-2024-37407 (libarchive RAR integer overflow -> double free)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: input forcing the dual-cleanup path. Diff-allocator detects the second free of a quarantined/already-freed chunk; CASR reports double-free/invalid-free. Strongly confirmable.
archetypes.fp_trap: Cleanup that nulls P after the first free, or distinct allocations that happen to share a variable across iterations. Suppress on intervening NULL-store or reassignment.

archetypes.name: realloc moves the buffer; a stale pointer/alias is used afterward
archetypes.pattern: After p = realloc(p, n) (or q = realloc(...)), code keeps using an OLD pointer or an interior pointer/alias that referenced the pre-realloc block, which realloc may have moved/freed. UAF on the old address.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: use of an alias A that was derived from P before a realloc(P) that returned a possibly-different pointer. Decompiled shape: A = P (or P+off) captured before realloc; realloc result stored to P; A used after. Slice: track aliases of the realloc input across the call; flag uses of pre-realloc aliases after the call. SHARPENING (uaf lens): model realloc as 'frees input, returns maybe-new'; any retained alias of the input pointer (including interior cursors into the buffer) used post-realloc is a UAF candidate. Pure free()-based UAF lenses miss realloc entirely — ADD realloc to the free-set.
grounding: CVE-2024-37407 / libarchive RAR window realloc class
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: force a realloc that relocates (grow past the bin), then exercise the stale-alias use. Diff-allocator always-moves-on-realloc makes this deterministic; CASR = heap-use-after-free. Excellent confirmable (a moving allocator is a known amplifier).
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that recomputes all interior pointers from the new base after realloc, or never aliases the input. Suppress when every post-realloc use derives from the realloc RESULT, not the pre-call pointer.

archetypes.name: Reference-count / ownership underflow leading to premature free + use
archetypes.pattern: An object's refcount is decremented too many times (double unref, unref on an error path that already unref'd), the object is freed while another holder still references it, then that holder uses it. Common in parser/object models and GLib/GObject-style code.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: use of an object after its refcount reaches 0 / its destructor ran. Decompiled shape: paired incref/decref helpers; a path with more decrefs than increfs followed by a use. Slice: harder statically; 0verse's edge is to fuzz the lifecycle and catch the use post-free dynamically. SHARPENING (uaf lens): treat resolvable unref/release/put helpers (that call free when count hits 0) as conditional frees; add them to the free-set so the dynamic UAF check covers refcounted objects, not just raw free().
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR (dynamic). Trigger: exercise the over-decref path then the surviving-reference use. Confirmable when the over-unref is reachable by input; classification = use-after-free. Note: needs the refcount logic to be input-drivable (sometimes deep).
archetypes.fp_trap: Balanced incref/decref; or decref helpers that null the local handle. Suppress when each decref path is matched by an incref on the same object, or the handle is cleared on release.

archetypes.name: Reentrancy / async-signal UAF (signal handler or callback frees shared state)
archetypes.pattern: A signal handler, timer, or reentrant callback calls async-signal-unsafe functions (free/malloc/syslog) while the main flow holds/uses the same heap state, corrupting the allocator or freeing in-use objects. The regreSSHion class.
archetypes.detection_signature: Decompiled shape: a signal()/sigaction() handler (or atexit/timer callback) that transitively calls free/malloc/syslog; the same allocations are live in the interrupted context. Slice: identify handlers registered via signal/sigaction and check whether they reach allocator/stdio calls (async-signal-unsafe). SHARPENING (uaf lens): add a 'signal-handler reaches free/malloc/syslog' static flag as a UAF/heap-corruption HINT (this is hard to PoV deterministically — mark as HYPOTHESIS-leaning, race-gated). Lower confidence than the deterministic UAF shapes.
grounding: CVE-2024-6387 (OpenSSH regreSSHion SIGALRM -> syslog -> malloc/free heap corruption)
CVE-2006-5051 (the original sshd signal-race it regressed from)
archetypes.confirmable: CASR under heavy timing/race fuzzing (NOT deterministic). Trigger: win the signal-delivery race during allocator activity. This is the LEAST oracle-confirmable userland archetype — note as HYPOTHESIS / race-gated; static flag is the primary deliverable, PoV is probabilistic.
archetypes.fp_trap: Handlers that only set a volatile sig_atomic_t flag and do no allocation/stdio (the correct pattern). Suppress when the handler does not reach any async-signal-unsafe allocator/stdio call.

archetypes.name: Dangling element pointer after container resize/removal
archetypes.pattern: Code holds a pointer/iterator into a dynamic container (vector/list/hashtable/string) and then an operation reallocates or removes from that container (push that grows it, erase, rehash), invalidating the held pointer, which is then dereferenced. C++ STL iterator-invalidation and C dynamic-array equivalents.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: deref of a captured interior pointer after a container-mutating call. Decompiled shape (C++): a pointer/reference obtained from vector::operator[]/data()/back(), then a push_back/insert/resize, then a use of the old pointer. In C: pointer into a buffer that is later realloc'd (overlaps UAF-03). Slice: capture-then-mutate-then-use of container-interior pointers. SHARPENING (uaf lens): for C++ targets, add known container-growth methods (push_back/insert/emplace/resize/rehash) to the 'invalidation' set alongside realloc; treat captured element pointers as freed across those calls.
grounding: CVE-2022-... Chromium/Skia container UAF (generalized C++ class)
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: cause the container to grow/rehash while the stale pointer is held, then use it. Deterministic with a moving allocator / poisoned freed storage.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that re-fetches the element pointer after every mutation, or reserves capacity up front so no reallocation occurs. Suppress when the pointer is re-derived after the mutating call.

archetypes.name: Parent/cache pointer to a freed child node (tree/graph parser)
archetypes.pattern: A parser/DOM/AST frees a child/sub-object but a parent node, cache, or back-reference still points to it; a later traversal dereferences the dangling link. Common in XML/HTML/font/media container parsers with object graphs.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: traversal deref of a stored pointer field after the pointee was freed. Decompiled shape: free of an object whose address was stored into another object's field (no subsequent null of that field), later loaded and dereferenced. Slice: escape-aware — when a freed pointer was stored into a longer-lived structure and that field is later read. SHARPENING (uaf lens): track 'freed pointer previously stored into a heap field' (not just stack locals); the dynamic check then catches traversal-time UAF. Requires modeling pointer escapes into structures.
archetypes.confirmable: differential-allocator + CASR. Trigger: input that frees a child then triggers a traversal through the stale parent link. Deterministic under quarantine allocator.
archetypes.fp_trap: Parsers that null the parent's link on child free, or use ownership/arena allocation freed all-at-once. Suppress when the back-reference field is cleared at free time, or the arena outlives all traversals.

archetypes.name: Attacker string reaches system()/popen() built via sprintf/strcat
archetypes.pattern: A command line is assembled (often with sprintf/strcat/asprintf) embedding attacker-controlled data (filename, hostname, parameter) and passed to system()/popen()/exec via /bin/sh -c. Shell metacharacters in the data inject commands.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink import: system/popen/execl(.../"/bin/sh","-c",...)/execlp. Decompiled shape: the command-string argument traces to a sprintf/strcat whose inputs include argv/getenv/recv/fread, with no shell-escaping/allowlist between. Slice: forward taint from input to the system/popen format. SHARPENING (cmdi lens): ensure the sink set includes popen, execl/execlp/execvp WHEN the program is a shell (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, sh -c), and asprintf/snprintf-built command buffers; taint sources MUST include getenv and argv, not only network. Detect the '/bin/sh','-c' immediate as a shell-exec marker.
archetypes.confirmable: Direct behavioral oracle (process-exec instrumentation) + CASR-style detection of an unexpected child process. Trigger: input containing ';id' or '`id`' or '$(...)'; observe the injected command run (e.g. a sentinel file/marker). HIGHLY confirmable — 0verse can ptrace/seccomp-trap execve of an unexpected program. NOT a memory oracle; needs an exec-trap oracle.
archetypes.fp_trap: Data passed via execve with an explicit argv vector (no shell) and no metacharacter interpretation; or strict allowlist/escaping (e.g. only [A-Za-z0-9_]). Suppress when the exec is shell-less argv AND the data cannot become a separate argv element, or when a sanitizer/allowlist dominates.

archetypes.name: Shell-exec of a filename/template field containing metacharacters
archetypes.pattern: A filename, URI, print-job attribute, or template string from input is handed to a shell (directly, or via a 'pipe'/template feature like %pipe%, |cmd, backticks in config) without neutralizing metacharacters. Filename-as-command.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: system/popen/execvp("sh",...) OR a fopen/open of a name starting with '|' (popen-style pipe-open). Decompiled shape: a tainted path/name reaches an exec OR a stdio open whose first char is checked for '|' (pipe device). Slice: taint to exec, plus a special rule for libraries that treat leading '|' / '%pipe%' as exec. SHARPENING (cmdi lens): add the 'pipe-open' idiom (popen-on-fopen, leading-'|' filename, '%pipe%' template) to the cmdi sink model — these are exec sinks that don't literally call system(). Many real CVEs hide here.
grounding: CVE-2022-... Perl/Ruby open('|cmd') class (generalized to C popen)
archetypes.confirmable: exec-trap oracle. Trigger: filename '|id' / '%pipe%id' / 'file;id'; observe the unexpected execve. Confirmable with process instrumentation; behavioral, not memory.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that opens the name with open(2)/fopen without ever invoking a shell and rejects leading '|'. Suppress when the open path cannot reach popen/exec and metachar/leading-pipe is filtered.

archetypes.name: Argument injection (attacker controls an argv element passed to a subprocess)
archetypes.pattern: Even without a shell, attacker data becomes a separate argument to a trusted program (git, tar, curl, ssh, find, openssl). A value starting with '-' is interpreted as an option/flag (e.g. '--upload-pack', '-o ProxyCommand', '--use-compress-program'), turning into command execution or file write.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: execv/execvp/execve/posix_spawn with an argv array where a tainted element is placed in an option position (or simply present as a standalone element). Decompiled shape: argv[i] = tainted; argv passed to exec of a known multi-option tool. Slice: taint into an argv element of a subprocess exec; raise even when there is NO shell. SHARPENING (cmdi lens): EXTEND beyond system()/shell — add argv-injection detection on execv*/posix_spawn; flag tainted argv elements (especially ones that can start with '-') to known dangerous-flag programs. Pure 'reaches system()' lenses miss the entire CWE-88 argument-injection class.
archetypes.confirmable: exec-trap oracle + effect observation. Trigger: a value like '--use-compress-program=id' or '-oProxyCommand=id'; observe the resulting command/side effect. Confirmable behaviorally; sometimes needs the target tool present.
archetypes.fp_trap: Code that inserts '--' before user args to stop option parsing, or validates that the value does not start with '-'. Suppress when a '--' separator or leading-dash rejection dominates the exec.

archetypes.name: Environment/config-derived value flows to exec (getenv -> system/exec)
archetypes.pattern: A value from getenv() (PATH, IFS, LD_*, a custom VAR), a config file, or a registry/PPD/template flows into system()/popen()/exec or into a constructed command. Includes untrusted-search-path and shell-via-env cases. Especially dangerous in setuid/privileged binaries.
archetypes.detection_signature: Sink: system/popen/exec with an argument/format influenced by getenv/config-read. Decompiled shape: getenv() result (or a config-parse buffer) flows to a command sink; in setuid context (geteuid != getuid hints) severity rises. Slice: taint from getenv/config to exec. SHARPENING (cmdi lens): add getenv and config-file reads as first-class cmdi TAINT SOURCES (not just argv/network); add a setuid/privileged-context modifier to prioritize. Detect IFS/PATH-style env reaching system().
archetypes.confirmable: exec-trap oracle. Trigger: set the env/config value to a payload, run, observe injected exec. Confirmable behaviorally when the env/config is reachable in the harness.
archetypes.fp_trap: Privileged programs that sanitize the environment (clearenv / explicit PATH) before exec, or use absolute paths and argv vectors. Suppress when env is scrubbed or the exec uses a fixed absolute program + argv.

archetypes.name: Unauth CGI param to system()/popen() command injection
archetypes.pattern: An unauthenticated web/CGI handler reads a request field (query string, POST body, Cookie, Host) via a vendor getter and passes it, unsanitized or with weak shell-metachar filtering, into system()/popen()/execve("/bin/sh","-c",...)/do_system()/twsystem(). Attacker injects `;`, `|`, `&`, `$()`, backticks to run arbitrary commands as root.
archetypes.detection_signature: PLT/imports of system, popen, execve, execlp, ___system, doSystem, twsystem, CsteSystem. Vendor param getters present as strings/PLT: websGetVar, webGetVar, get_cgi, fcgi_get_query, nvram_get, nvram_safe_get, GetValue, websGetVarN, sub_get_value, json_object_get_string. Decompile shape: getter() return value flows (often via sprintf into a cmd buffer) directly into system(cmd) with no execve-style argv split and no allow-list. Lens fires when a taint source (request getter) reaches a shell sink in the same/adjacent function. MIPS: `lw $t9,%call16(system)($gp); jalr $t9` with $a0 built by sprintf; arg in $a0. ARM: `bl system` / `bl popen` with r0 = sprintf dest. Watch for sprintf(buf,"... %s ...",param) immediately preceding the sink (command template).
grounding: CVE-2023-1389 (TP-Link Archer AX21 country param -> popen)
CVE-2024-7261 (Zyxel AP/router host param in cookie)
archetypes.confirmable: YES - highest confirmability. cmdi canary: hook/wrap system/popen/execve in Qiling so any invocation whose argument contains an injected canary token (e.g. `;echo PWNK_$RAND`) trips the oracle. Trigger = single crafted HTTP request to the handler. Emulation needs: webserver bootstrapped enough to dispatch (or direct call of the handler with a faked CGI env / QUERY_STRING), plus nvram_get/nvram_safe_get stubs returning benign defaults so init doesn't bail. No real rootfs services required.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, network-reachable (HTTP/HTTPS on LAN, sometimes WAN). Highest-impact firmware bug class.

archetypes.name: strcpy of HTTP/nvram value into fixed stack buffer
archetypes.pattern: A request field or nvram value is copied with strcpy/strcat/memcpy(no bound) into a fixed-size stack array. Oversized input overflows the saved return address / saved registers, giving control of PC. Classic SOHO router web-handler shape.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: strcpy, strcat, memcpy, bcopy. Source: websGetVar/nvram_get/recv. Decompile shape: local char buf[N] (N small, 16-256) with strcpy(buf, attacker_str) and no prior strlen()/length check. Stack-canary absence is common (no __stack_chk_fail import). MIPS: spot the stack frame size (addiu $sp,$sp,-N) vs copy length; overwrite target is saved $ra at top of frame. Big-endian (Broadcom) vs little-endian (Realtek/Atheros) changes payload but not the lens. ARM: store of attacker bytes past the buffer onto saved {fp,lr}. Lens: bounded-vs-unbounded copy where dest is a stack slot and the source is request-tainted.
grounding: Tenda CX12L/RX3 setSchedWifi schedStartTime/schedEndTime into 25-byte buffer
CVE-2026-34124 (TP-Link HTTP GET realpath stack BOF)
archetypes.confirmable: YES (well-suited). Qiling oracle: invoke the handler with an over-long field and detect crash via PC = attacker pattern (cyclic), invalid fetch at controlled address, or write past mapped stack. Needs the webserver/handler reachable and nvram stubs; for a single non-stateful handler you can call the function directly with a synthesized request struct. No full rootfs needed for the corruption itself.
archetypes.reachability_note: Often UNAUTH on /goform, /boaform, /cgi-bin endpoints; some require a session. Network-reachable LAN, sometimes WAN-exposed httpd.

archetypes.name: sprintf into fixed buffer with attacker data
archetypes.pattern: sprintf/vsprintf builds a string into a fixed buffer using one or more attacker-controlled %s fields (request params, headers). Combined length exceeds the buffer -> stack/global overflow. Distinct from cmdi: the sprintf result need not reach a shell; the overflow itself is the bug. Frequently the same sprintf is also the command-template feeding system() (combo bug).
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: sprintf, vsprintf, swprintf (no snprintf/bound). Decompile: sprintf(fixed_buf, fmt_with_%s, tainted...) where total runtime length is unchecked. Look for format strings in .rodata like "%s/%s", "cmd=%s", "/bin/ping %s". MIPS: format string ptr in $a1, dest in $a0; the %s args in $a2/$a3/stack. ARM: r0=dest, r1=fmt, r2+=args. Lens: unbounded format function whose dest is fixed-size and any %s arg is request-tainted.
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Same Qiling approach as strcpy-stack: oversized %s argument -> corruption detected by crash/PC control. cmdi canary catches it too if the sprintf result feeds a shell.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH or auth depending on endpoint; network-reachable.

archetypes.name: Missing auth on sensitive endpoint / auth bypass
archetypes.pattern: A sensitive handler (config get/set, firmware upload, factory reset, telnet enable, getcfg) is reachable without authentication because the auth check is keyed on URL prefix/extension allow-list, a path-traversal slips past the check, or the session check is missing entirely on that route. Turns an authed bug into a pre-auth one.
archetypes.detection_signature: Look for the dispatch table / URL router (string table of paths mapped to handler fn pointers) and the auth gate function (checks session cookie / token, often strcmp/strstr on a referer or path). Detection: handler fn pointers that are NOT dominated by the auth-check call, or auth decided by string-prefix match (strncmp(path,"/login",6), strstr(uri,".cgi")) that a crafted path bypasses. getcfg/hedwig.cgi-style routes leaking XML config (creds). MIPS/ARM: trace whether the auth function's return is branched on before reaching the handler call; an unconditional handler call = missing auth.
grounding: TP-Link Archer NX (unauth firmware upload, missing HTTP auth)
D-Link DIR-859 hedwig.cgi getcfg path traversal -> config/cred disclosure
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL. Reaching the handler without a session is confirmable by emulating the dispatch + auth gate and observing the handler fires with no/empty cookie. But proving the security impact (which config/creds leak) needs a fuller rootfs so the handler can read real nvram/config files. cmdi canary still applies if the now-reachable handler also has a shell sink.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH (that is the whole point). Network-reachable; severity depends on what the endpoint does.

archetypes.name: Path traversal in CGI file/service param
archetypes.pattern: A request param naming a file/service/template is concatenated into a filesystem path and opened/read/written with no canonicalization, allowing ../ to read config (with plaintext creds), arbitrary files, or write to overwrite scripts.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: fopen, open, sprintf (to build path), strcat. Decompile: sprintf(path,"/htdocs/webinc/getcfg/%s", param) or strcat(base, param) then fopen(path). No realpath()/'..' rejection. Strings: "/htdocs/", "/var/", "/tmp/", ".xml". Lens: request-tainted string concatenated into a path used by a file API without a traversal filter. MIPS/ARM: param getter -> sprintf path -> fopen, all in one handler.
grounding: QNAP QHora-322 path traversal (Pwn2Own Ireland 2024 chain)
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL. Confirmable in Qiling only with a populated rootfs (the target config files must exist) so the traversal resolves and returns content. The path-construction sink is statically detectable; runtime proof needs the filesystem.
archetypes.reachability_note: Often UNAUTH; network-reachable. High value as info-leak primitive in a chain (leak creds -> auth -> RCE).

archetypes.name: Format string from request field into printf/syslog
archetypes.pattern: An attacker-controlled string is passed as the FORMAT argument to printf/sprintf/syslog/fprintf (e.g. syslog(LOG_INFO, user_agent)). %n/%s/%x give read/write primitives and crashes. Common in logging of hostnames, User-Agent, login names.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: printf, fprintf, sprintf, snprintf, syslog, vsnprintf. Decompile: the FIRST format arg is a tainted register rather than a .rodata string pointer. MIPS: $a0 (printf) or $a1 (sprintf/syslog level then fmt) loaded from a request getter instead of an address in .rodata. ARM: r0/r1 fmt arg sourced from tainted data. Lens: format-family call whose format-position argument is not a constant string literal but request-tainted. Easy to spot: constant-format calls have a `lui/addiu` or `ldr =addr` into the fmt slot; tainted ones load from a variable.
grounding: Embedded camera web logging of attacker hostname
archetypes.confirmable: YES (lightweight). Qiling oracle: send a field containing %n/%x and detect a crash or out-of-bounds access from the varargs walk; or hook printf-family and flag when the format arg is in attacker-tainted memory. Minimal rootfs needed if you can reach the logging path.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH if the logged field is pre-auth (User-Agent, login name, hostname). Network-reachable.

archetypes.name: sscanf %s of HTTP header/path into fixed buffer
archetypes.pattern: Pre-auth request parsing uses sscanf(input, "...%s...", buf) or %[ with no width specifier into a fixed buffer, overflowing it. Common in HTTP request-line / header / Content-Length / Range / boundary parsing in the webserver core before auth runs.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: sscanf, __isoc99_sscanf. Decompile: sscanf(headerbuf, "%s"/"%[^ ]"/"%d %s", localbuf) with localbuf fixed-size and no %.Ns width. Format strings in .rodata like "%[^:]:%s", "GET %s", "Content-Length: %d". MIPS/ARM: trace the destination register (varargs) to a stack slot smaller than possible input. Lens: scanf-family with unbounded %s/%[ writing a fixed stack buffer from network data.
grounding: CVE-2025-40596/40597 (SonicWall SMA100 pre-auth sscanf/stack & heap overflows)
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Qiling: feed an over-long header/request line, detect stack corruption / PC control. The webserver request-parse path is reachable pre-auth, so emulation only needs the parser bootstrapped (often a tight loop you can call directly).
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, network-reachable - it is in the request parser before any auth. High value.

archetypes.name: Pre-auth HTTP header/Cookie/Host parse overflow
archetypes.pattern: The webserver core copies or parses an HTTP header value (Cookie, Host, Authorization, Content-Length-driven body, Referer) into a fixed buffer before authentication, overflowing on long input or mis-trusting an attacker length field.
archetypes.detection_signature: In the httpd accept/parse loop: recv -> header tokenizer (strchr/strtok on ':' '\r\n') -> strcpy/memcpy into fixed buffers per header. Look for memcpy(dst, body, content_length) where content_length is the attacker's value with no cap. Imports: recv, strstr, strtok, strncpy(misused), memcpy. MIPS/ARM: the parse loop sits right after accept()/recv(); buffers are stack or a fixed global request struct.
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Same as sscanf/strcpy oracle: malformed header -> crash. Reachable pre-auth in the parse loop.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, network-reachable, pre-auth in the server core. Highest-impact.

archetypes.name: UPnP/SOAP action param to cmdi or overflow
