archetypes.pattern: A UPnP/SOAP service (miniupnpd, Realtek/Broadcom UPnP, AddPortMapping/SetDefaultConnectionService) reads an action argument (NewInternalClient, NewPortMappingDescription, device descriptor) and feeds it to system()/iptables shell calls or copies it unbounded. Often UNAUTH on UDP 1900 / the SOAP control URL.
archetypes.detection_signature: Strings: "urn:schemas-upnp-org", "AddPortMapping", "NewInternalClient", "SetupReady", SOAPAction. Imports: system/popen near iptables/ebtables string templates, or strcpy of SOAP arg. Realtek eCos SDK signatures (UDPServer, formAddDhcps). Decompile: XML/SOAP arg extracted then sprintf'd into an iptables/route command or copied to a fixed buffer. MIPS/ARM: the SOAP dispatcher maps action name -> handler; trace arg -> sink.
grounding: CVE-2021-35394 (Realtek Jungle SDK UDPServer/UPnP multiple overflow+cmdi, mass-exploited)
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL-to-YES. cmdi canary catches the iptables/system path if you can drive a SOAP request into the daemon under Qiling (needs the UDP/HTTP listener and minimal nvram). Overflow variant confirmable via crash. Daemon often forks/uses sockets -> needs more emulation scaffolding than a single CGI call.
archetypes.reachability_note: Frequently UNAUTH; LAN-reachable, historically WAN-exposed. Mass-exploited class (Mirai/RondoDox).

archetypes.name: Custom TCP/UDP management daemon command injection
archetypes.pattern: A vendor management/discovery daemon on a custom port (TP-Link tdpServer UDP 20002, Tenda/Realtek config daemons, Netis 53413) parses a proprietary message and passes a field to system()/popen(). Often UNAUTH and reachable on LAN.
archetypes.detection_signature: Non-httpd binary bound to a fixed UDP/TCP port (look for bind()/htons(constant) in the daemon). Custom message parser (magic bytes, TLV) then a field -> sprintf -> system(). Strings: vendor magic, "slp", port constants. Imports: recvfrom, system, popen. MIPS/ARM: recvfrom buffer -> field extract -> shell sink.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL-to-YES. cmdi canary applies once the message reaches the sink. Needs the daemon's socket loop emulated (Qiling can feed recvfrom from a scripted buffer) + nvram stubs. More scaffolding than CGI but no real network.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, LAN-reachable (sometimes WAN). High value.

archetypes.name: Telnet/debug backdoor with hardcoded creds on WAN
archetypes.pattern: Firmware starts telnetd/a debug shell (sometimes only when WAN link comes up) and authenticates against hardcoded credentials or a magic command, giving root. Or a hidden 'utelnetd'/'dbglog' service with a static password.
archetypes.detection_signature: Strings: literal usernames/passwords, "telnetd", "utelnetd", "/bin/login -f", "Alphanetworks", vendor signing strings near a strcmp. Imports: system("telnetd"), strcmp(input, "<const>"). Detection: a strcmp/memcmp of a network-supplied credential against a constant string in .rodata; or a service-start of telnetd gated on a link/event. MIPS/ARM: constant string operand in the compare = the hardcoded secret.
grounding: CVE-2024-45697 (D-Link DIR-X4860 telnet on WAN, hardcoded creds)
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL (mostly static). The hardcoded credential and the service-start are statically detectable with high confidence (string + strcmp). Runtime confirmation in Qiling means emulating the login path; the value is already proven by the static constant. Good string/strcmp lens hit, low emulation need.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH (the creds ARE the backdoor); WAN-reachable in the worst cases. Root.

archetypes.name: DHCP/DNS/option parser overflow in network daemon
archetypes.pattern: udhcpd/udhcpc/dnsmasq-like daemon copies an attacker-supplied option (hostname option 12, DHCP client-id, DNS name label) into a fixed buffer without bounding the option length field, overflowing. Reachable from LAN as a rogue client/server.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: memcpy, strcpy near option-parsing loops (read length byte then copy length bytes). Decompile: `len = opt[1]; memcpy(buf, opt+2, len)` with buf fixed and len attacker-controlled. Strings: "udhcpd", "dnsmasq", option numbers. MIPS/ARM: TLV walk (ptr += 2 + len) with the copy length from the packet.
grounding: Various udhcpd/udhcpc option-12 hostname overflows in BusyBox-derived stacks
dnsmasq DNS name parse CVEs (DNSpooq family)
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Qiling: feed a crafted DHCP/DNS packet to the parse function; detect overflow crash. The option parser is usually a pure function you can call directly with a packet buffer (no sockets needed).
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, LAN-reachable (link-local). Lower exposure than HTTP but real.

archetypes.name: TR-069/CWMP/SNMP parameter handling overflow or injection
archetypes.pattern: The CWMP (TR-069) client or SNMP agent copies a server/OID-supplied value (ParameterValue, ACS URL, SNMP SET community/string) into a fixed buffer or into a shell call. ACS-side or rogue-ACS attacker controls input.
archetypes.detection_signature: Strings: "cwmp", "InternalProductClass", "ACS", "snmpd", OID strings. Imports: strcpy/sprintf of ParameterValue, system() of a config value applied from CWMP. SOAP/XML parse then copy. MIPS/ARM: trace ParameterValue extraction -> sink.
grounding: Various TR-069/CWMP RCE (Cable Haunt-adjacent, Mirai TR-069 worm)
SNMP SET overflow in embedded agents
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL. Needs the CWMP/SNMP daemon and a scripted server message; more stateful. cmdi canary applies if a CWMP value reaches system(). Static detection solid; runtime needs scaffolding.
archetypes.reachability_note: Auth varies (CWMP trusts the ACS; rogue-ACS or MITM); often WAN-side. Medium reachability.

archetypes.name: TLV/length-field integer overflow to heap overflow
archetypes.pattern: A binary protocol parser reads a length/count field, performs arithmetic (len-1, len*elem, len+hdr) that wraps or underflows, then allocates/copies based on the bad value -> heap overflow. Canonical baseband/IoT-protocol shape.
archetypes.detection_signature: Decompile: read 16/32-bit field from packet -> arithmetic -> malloc/memcpy. Red flags: malloc(len * n) without overflow check, memcpy(dst, src, len - k), signed/unsigned mix on the length. Imports: malloc, memcpy. MIPS/ARM: load (lhu/lh, big-endian on many basebands) the length, then a multiply/subtract feeding move into $a2/r2 of memcpy. Lens: allocation or copy size derived by arithmetic from a packet field with no bounds/overflow guard.
grounding: CVE-2023-21517 (Samsung baseband LTE ESM TFT IE heap overflow)
CVE-2023-26073 (Samsung 5G NAS extended emergency number list)
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY in the firmware lane. Detectable with high confidence in Ghidra (the wrap/underflow shape). NOT confirmable in the Qiling CGI/router oracle: baseband requires a dedicated emulator (FirmWire/ShannonEmu) modelling the RTOS, mailboxes and RF stack. Flag as 'detect, hand to specialist emulator', do not claim Qiling confirmation.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH, OVER-THE-AIR (rogue base station) for baseband; for IoT TLV daemons it is network-reachable. Critical impact, hard to confirm.

archetypes.name: Copy-before-validate / reassembly off-by-one
archetypes.pattern: A fragment/segment reassembler copies fragment data into a buffer in a loop and checks the exit/overflow condition AFTER the copy, or trusts a per-fragment length that diverges from the allocation length, overflowing the reassembly buffer.
archetypes.detection_signature: Decompile: a loop `while(more){ memcpy(dst+off, frag, frag_len); off+=frag_len; if(off>max) break; }` (check after copy). Two different length variables for allocate vs copy. Imports: memcpy in a loop with a running offset. MIPS/ARM: loop with accumulating offset register; the bound compare is post-copy. Lens: monotonic-offset copy loop where the guard does not dominate the write.
grounding: CVE-2023-41112/41111 (Samsung Exynos GPRS LLC reassembly heap overflow)
TCP/IP stack reassembly bugs in embedded stacks
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY for baseband (same emulator caveat as TLV). For an embedded-Linux reassembler (IP frag, file-format), the loop is a callable pure function -> Qiling CAN drive it with crafted fragments and detect the overflow. Confirmability depends on whether the parser is OS-level (yes) or baseband RTOS (no).
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH/OTA or network-reachable. Critical.

archetypes.name: Signed/negative length in memcpy from packet field
archetypes.pattern: A length read as signed (or computed as remaining = total - consumed going negative) is passed to memcpy/read, which treats it as a huge size_t -> massive overread/overwrite. A pervasive embedded-parser footgun.
archetypes.detection_signature: Decompile: signed int length compared with `<= max` only (no `>= 0` lower bound), then used as memcpy size. MIPS/ARM: sign-extending load (lb/lh, not lbu/lhu) of a length, or a subtraction that can go negative, feeding the size arg. Lens: memcpy/memmove/read size argument that is a signed value lacking a lower-bound check.
grounding: Baseband and IoT length-handling CVEs (shared root cause)
archetypes.confirmable: YES for OS-level parsers (callable function + crafted buffer in Qiling -> overread/overwrite crash). STATIC-ONLY when inside baseband. Lens is cheap and high-signal.
archetypes.reachability_note: Depends on host parser; generally network-reachable, often UNAUTH.

archetypes.name: Config/NVRAM backup-restore blob parser overflow
archetypes.pattern: The 'restore configuration' / import-backup handler parses an attacker-supplied .cfg/.bin/.dat blob (often XOR/weakly encrypted) and copies fields into fixed structs or applies values without validation -> overflow or stored injection. The blob format is reverse-engineered from the same binary.
archetypes.detection_signature: Find the restore handler (string "restore", "config.bin", "NVRAM", "backup"). Decompile: read header magic -> loop copying TLV entries into nvram_set or fixed buffers. Imports: memcpy, nvram_set, the vendor decrypt routine (look for a hardcoded XOR/AES key nearby). MIPS/ARM: blob field -> struct copy with no bound.
archetypes.confirmable: YES (auth permitting). Qiling: feed a crafted config blob to the restore parser; detect overflow or, if values reach system()/nvram-then-system, the cmdi canary fires. Needs the decrypt key (extractable from the binary) and nvram_set stubs.
archetypes.reachability_note: Usually AUTHED (upload via admin UI) -> lower severity, but chains with auth bypass. Network-reachable.

archetypes.name: Multipart/XML/JSON upload boundary parser overflow
archetypes.pattern: The multipart/form-data, XML, or JSON parser in the webserver copies a boundary token, filename, field name, or value into a fixed buffer without bounding -> pre/post-auth overflow during upload handling.
archetypes.detection_signature: Strings: "Content-Disposition", "boundary=", "multipart/form-data", "filename=". Decompile: strstr/strchr to locate boundary -> strcpy/memcpy of the delimited region into a fixed buffer. Imports: strstr, memcpy, strcpy. MIPS/ARM: the body scan loop with a fixed destination.
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Qiling: craft a multipart body with an over-long boundary/filename, detect crash. Reachable pre-auth if upload parsing precedes auth (common). Webserver bootstrap + nvram stubs.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH if pre-auth multipart parsing; else authed. Network-reachable.

archetypes.name: nvram_get value used unsanitized in system()
archetypes.pattern: A config value previously settable via the web UI/API/CWMP is read with nvram_get and concatenated into a shell command at apply time (e.g. building iptables/route/ping/ddns commands). A second-order/stored command injection: the malicious value is set in one request, executed when config is applied/rebooted.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: nvram_get/nvram_safe_get/nvram_bufget + system/popen. Decompile: nvram_get("<key>") -> sprintf into a command -> system(). The taint source is nvram, not the immediate request, so single-function lenses miss it - need a cross-cutting 'nvram value reaches shell' lens that pairs the SET path (websGetVar->nvram_set) with the APPLY path (nvram_get->system). Strings: nvram keys like "ddns_hostname", "wan_ifname", "lan_ipaddr". MIPS/ARM: same shell-sink shape, different source.
archetypes.confirmable: YES with nvram model. cmdi canary catches it IF the emulation makes nvram_get return an attacker-chosen value (your nvram stub must be writable: set the key to `;echo CANARY`, then drive the apply path). Two-step trigger. No real rootfs services needed beyond the nvram model.
archetypes.reachability_note: Often AUTHED to set the value, but the value may be settable via a separate UNAUTH endpoint or default; network-reachable. Common Mirai vector.

archetypes.name: nvram_set / oversized value into fixed config struct
archetypes.pattern: An oversized config value is copied into a fixed-size field of an in-memory config struct or stack buffer during set/apply (strcpy(cfg->field, nvram_get(key))), overflowing adjacent fields or the stack.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: strcpy/memcpy with dest = a struct field of known size and src = nvram_get/websGetVar. Decompile: per-key copy into a typed config struct without length cap. MIPS/ARM: struct base + offset store loop. Lens: bounded-vs-unbounded copy where dest is a config-struct field.
grounding: Tenda/D-Link nvram field overflows in apply handlers
archetypes.confirmable: YES. Qiling: set an over-long nvram value (writable stub) and drive apply; detect corruption. Same scaffolding as stored-cmdi.
archetypes.reachability_note: Usually AUTHED set; network-reachable; chains with auth bypass.

archetypes.name: Hardcoded credentials / keys in defaults or binary
archetypes.pattern: Default admin credentials, an undocumented support account, a magic 'master' password, API keys, or private keys are embedded in the binary or the default nvram set, granting access or enabling firmware/traffic decryption.
archetypes.detection_signature: String scan for credential-shaped constants near a strcmp/memcmp on a network/login input, or in the nvram-default table (init function that nvram_set's many keys). Imports: strcmp/memcmp(input, const), and crypto with a fixed key buffer in .rodata. The 'backdoor account' shape = a hidden username compared before/around the normal auth. MIPS/ARM: constant operand of the compare is the secret; default-table = sequence of addiu/move with .rodata string args into nvram_set.
grounding: CVE-2024-3272 (D-Link NAS hardcoded 'messagebus' account, no password)
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY (and that is enough). The constant + its use in an auth compare is provable in Ghidra without emulation. Qiling can demo login with the recovered cred but adds little; this is a string/compare lens, near-zero emulation need.
archetypes.reachability_note: UNAUTH (the creds bypass auth). Network-reachable; severity = whatever the account can do (often root).

archetypes.name: Config value used as path/format without validation
archetypes.pattern: An nvram/config value is used to build a filesystem path, a library/script load path, or a format string at apply time, enabling traversal, arbitrary file write, or format-string abuse via a stored value.
archetypes.detection_signature: nvram_get -> fopen/exec path, or nvram_get used as printf/sprintf format. Same lenses as path-traversal and format-string but with an nvram source. Strings: nvram keys feeding "/tmp/%s", script names. MIPS/ARM: nvram value reaches a file API or format slot.
archetypes.confirmable: PARTIAL. Path variant needs a rootfs to demonstrate; format variant catchable by the printf hook. Static detection solid.
archetypes.reachability_note: Usually AUTHED set; network-reachable; second-order.

archetypes.name: Missing/weak firmware signature verification
archetypes.pattern: The update handler verifies the image with only CRC32/MD5 (or nothing), or checks integrity but not authenticity, so an attacker who can deliver an image (MITM of the update URL, or local upload) flashes arbitrary firmware -> persistent root.
archetypes.detection_signature: Find the verify routine in the update path (strings: "upgrade", "sysupgrade", "image", "signature", "verify"). Imports present: crc32, MD5_Init -> WEAK; absent RSA/EC verify (no mbedtls/openssl verify, no ECDSA/RSA_verify import) -> no authenticity. Decompile: header magic + length + checksum compared, then write to mtd/flash; no public-key check. MIPS/ARM: trace from image-receive to flash-write and inventory which integrity primitive gates it.
grounding: USENIX Sec'24 firmware-update study (39% CRC, 23.8% MD5)
TP-Link WR-series (RSA sig does not cover header)
Numerous SOHO devices with CRC-only images
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY (mostly). Detectable with high confidence by inventorying crypto primitives in the update path. Runtime confirmation = emulating the updater to accept a forged image, which needs the flash/mtd model -> heavier; static call-graph evidence is the deliverable.
archetypes.reachability_note: AUTHED upload, or UNAUTH via MITM of an HTTP update URL / unauth upload endpoint. Persistent root impact.

archetypes.name: Signature-check bypass via unsigned region / header redirect
archetypes.pattern: Authenticity IS checked, but the verifier reads metadata (signing table, fwmap, length, offset) from a part of the image the signature does NOT cover, letting the attacker point verification at attacker-controlled data and pass with a malicious payload.
archetypes.detection_signature: Decompile the verify routine: does it locate the signed-data range using a length/offset/table pointer taken from the unsigned header? Look for: parse header table -> hash range [a,b] where a/b come from the image -> verify. The signed region being defined by unsigned bytes is the bug. MIPS/ARM: the offsets feeding the hash loop are loaded from the image rather than fixed constants.
grounding: CVE-2025-7937 / CVE-2025-6198 (Supermicro BMC fake fwmap/signing table in unsigned region)
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY. This is a logic flaw provable by reading the verify routine; emulation adds little and needs the full updater. High-confidence static lens (crypto-coverage analysis), not a Qiling-canary target.
archetypes.reachability_note: AUTHED/local or MITM depending on delivery. Persistent root, defeats secure boot.

archetypes.name: Command injection in update/restore/upgrade handler
archetypes.pattern: The upgrade/restore handler passes an attacker-influenced filename, update URL, or version string to a shell (system("wget "+url), system("tar -xf "+name), sysupgrade wrapper) -> command injection during update.
archetypes.detection_signature: Imports: system/popen near update strings ("wget", "curl", "tar", "mtd", "sysupgrade", "fwupdate"). Decompile: sprintf(cmd,"wget %s",url)/("tar -xzf /tmp/%s",fname) -> system(cmd) with url/fname from the request. MIPS/ARM: standard shell-sink shape in the update code path.
grounding: Router 'check for update' URL injection cases
archetypes.confirmable: YES. cmdi canary catches it: drive the update/restore endpoint with a filename/URL containing `;echo CANARY`. Needs the handler reachable + nvram stubs; no real flash needed since the injection fires before/around the flash op.
archetypes.reachability_note: AUTHED typically; UNAUTH if the update-check endpoint is unauth or MITM-able. Network-reachable.

archetypes.name: Hardcoded firmware encryption/decryption key
archetypes.pattern: Encrypted firmware images are protected by a symmetric key embedded in the bootloader/updater binary. Recovering the key lets an attacker decrypt (to find more bugs) and, combined with weak authenticity, re-encrypt a forged image the device will accept.
archetypes.detection_signature: Find the decrypt routine in the updater (AES/DES/XOR). Imports: AES_set_decrypt_key, EVP_DecryptInit, or a hand-rolled XOR. The key is a fixed 16/24/32-byte buffer in .rodata or built by constant stores. MIPS/ARM: constant key bytes loaded into the cipher context; IV often fixed too. Lens: symmetric-crypto init whose key argument points to a constant.
grounding: Many vendors ship a single static AES key across a product line
Combined with CRC-only authenticity -> forge accepted images
archetypes.confirmable: STATIC-ONLY (and decisive). The key is recoverable directly from the binary; you can then decrypt offline. No Qiling needed to PROVE the key; emulating the decrypt to validate the key is a cheap optional cross-check.
archetypes.reachability_note: Not a remote bug by itself; an enabler/analysis primitive that, with weak signing, becomes persistent-root. Local/supply-chain.
